**Triage: `domain:spec`; `priority:p2`. ⚠️ The landing surface depends on one measurement the dev must take FIRST.**

`realtime-protocol.mdx` documents **four WebSocket message types `WebSocketMessageType` does not declare** — `auth`, `auth_success`, `auth_error`, `subscribed` — measured on `origin/main` `fd5cff209f` against `packages/spec/src/api/websocket.zod.ts:38`.

### The fork, and it decides the whole card

⛔ Do not assume the docs are wrong. Two readings, and only a measurement separates them:

1. **The runtime really sends these four** ⇒ the **contract is incomplete**; `WebSocketMessageType` must declare them, and the docs are right. This is the serious case: a client written against the declared enum cannot handle messages the server actually sends.
2. **Nothing sends them** ⇒ the **docs teach a vocabulary that does not exist** ⇒ correct the page, under objectstack#17031's standing ruling that doc-vs-implementation drift is fixed in the doc.

⇒ **Measure which, before writing anything.** Look for producers of each of the four. ⭐ Report the answer even if it turns out to be reading 2 — the enumeration is the deliverable either way.

⚠️ If it is reading 1, declaring four new members **widens a published enum** ⇒ Clause-② applies and must be declared; and the client-side consequence should be stated in the PR.

⛔ Not in scope: #16935's `type: "error"` flattening, which correctly fenced the `auth_error` fence out and asked for it to be measured — this card is that measurement, widened to the class it revealed.

`Size/model suggestion:` M — the measurement is the work; the edit is small either way.

### ⭐ The fork — decide it by measurement, and ⛔ only one branch is yours

`WebSocketMessageType` (`packages/spec/src/api/websocket.zod.ts:38`) declares a **closed** vocabulary, and `BaseWebSocketMessage` types its `type` against it — so a message outside that enum parses against **no** schema in the file. The page teaches four types that are not in it.

- **(a) The PAGE is wrong** — it documents a protocol the platform does not implement. Fix the prose. **This is your branch.**
- **(b) The ENUM is wrong** — those four are real and the declaration is missing them. ⛔ **NOT yours.** Adding a member to a published enum **widens a published payload**, flips clause ② to `yes`, and is a protocol decision. If your measurements point there, **stop and report** — ⛔ do not add the members, and ⛔ do not write prose that implies they are coming.

⚠️ It may be **split** — some of the four real-but-undeclared, others pure documentation fiction. ⭐ **Judge each of the four separately and say so per type**; ⛔ do not apply one verdict to all four because it is tidier.

### What to falsify first

⛔ Anchors **by state on `origin/main`**, never from the card (its reading is `fd5cff209f`):

1. `WebSocketMessageType` still declares exactly the ten members the card lists — read it, ⛔ do not inherit the list.
2. `BaseWebSocketMessage` still types `type` against that enum — this is what makes an undeclared type unparseable, and the whole argument rests on it. If it has loosened, the premise is void: **stop and report**.
3. The page still teaches all four — anchor **by content**, ⛔ not by line.
4. ⭐ **For each of the four, search the runtime for a producer or consumer.** A type the server actually emits is evidence for fork (b) and ⇒ **stop and report**; one with no producer anywhere is documentation fiction ⇒ fork (a). ⚠️ Give this a **lit control**: a declared type (`ping`, say) must show producers under the same probe. A search that finds nothing for everything proves nothing.

A stop-and-report backed by evidence is a **good outcome**, not a failed round.

### ⛔ Commit message — this cost two full rounds today

No card trailer of any kind: no `Part of`, `Part-of`, `Refs`, `Fixes`, `Closes`, `Resolves`, no bare `#17184`. Per **#17606** the discharge is **unreachable** at this repo's merge settings, so the red never clears. ⛔ No amend / rebase / force-push; a cosmetic commit on top only joins the commit list.

⭐ **Grep the message BEFORE pushing** — each → **0** via `grep -oiE | wc -l` (⛔ not `grep -c`), plus `#[0-9]+` → 0, lit controls `Co-Authored-By` → 1 and `Claude-Session` → 1. ⚠️ Count bare stems `Fix` / `Close` / `Resolve` separately — rounds today were bitten by `Closes` inside `findClosestMatches` and by `fix` inside `fixture`. Then run `scripts/check-partof-closing-keyword.mjs` on your commit **and** a known-bad one: yours exit 0, bad exit 1. ⭐ **Audit the PR BODY for stray closing keywords too.**

`Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`
`Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01MkQhmuuJAVDjmeWNixwDDH`

### ⭐ Instrument discipline

**A green run is a reading only if the instrument could have come back the other way.** Every zero needs a lit control. ⚠️ `grep -c` counts LINES — use `grep -o | wc -l`. ⚠️ A phrase can **wrap a line break**; flatten whitespace, and for a JSDoc/block comment strip the leading `*` per line first. ⚠️ Enumerate a file universe with `git ls-files` and **sanity-check the count** — a round today got 399 from a glob that silently dropped three pages. ⛔ Never grep file CONTENTS for a file NAME. ⛔ A `git grep` over a tree carrying built `dist/` is non-reproducible. ⛔ Report a discarded run; a prerequisite refusal is not a red and is not always exit 3.

### Gate declaration and the PR body

The gate defines it as *"this PR puts a **new key** on a published payload"* — a docs fix adds none, which is exactly why fork (b) would change the answer. ⚠️ Put `- **Clause-②: no**` on its own line in the PR BODY, validated with `readClause2Line` (⛔ not a string match; a heading `## Clause-② …` is a near miss).

⚠️ **Changeset**: decide on the repo's own rule and **state the rule with a measurement** (a `content/docs/**` path ships from no released package ⇒ `skip-changeset`; ⛔ do not assume). ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Draft PR, `Part of #17184` **in the body only**.
